title: v2 stores (seeded): a log read never fails on a line still being written
head: d44018462733ff9d6c6f71fd401237822d8dfa2d
brief: _read_lines reads an append-only JSONL log without the writer's lock. Only the last line, and only when the file does not end in a newline, can be a write in progress; if it does not parse (or ends mid-character) it is left out. Everything else stays an error: an interior or newline-terminated bad line is corruption and raises StoreError with a path:N: message. Records end at the newline only (U+2028 and friends are data). Tests: torn_read and separator_characters in tests/v2/stores_check.py.
focus: correctness, including under concurrency and across the ordering of events
handling of untrusted input, and safety-boundary changes
test coverage of the new behaviour: would the tests fail without the change?
claims in the description against the evidence in the diff and tests

seeded.description: the cut-multibyte branch of _read_lines slices up to the last newline's index instead of just past it, which breaks a log whose only line is still being written
seeded.patch:
diff --git a/jarvis/v2/stores.py b/jarvis/v2/stores.py
index 2b49e312..32094527 100644
--- a/jarvis/v2/stores.py
+++ b/jarvis/v2/stores.py
@@ -124,7 +124,7 @@ def _read_lines(path: Path) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
                 and exc.reason == "unexpected end of data" and exc.end == len(raw)
                 and exc.start > raw.rfind(b"\n")):
             try:                   # everything up to the last whole line
-                text = raw[:raw.rfind(b"\n") + 1].decode("utf-8")
+                text = raw[:raw.rfind(b"\n")].decode("utf-8")
             except UnicodeError as inner:
                 raise StoreError(f"{path}: {inner}") from inner
             unfinished = False     # the cut line is gone; what is left ends in a newline

ground_truth.mechanism: when the unterminated tail ends mid-character, the fallback keeps 'everything up to the last whole line' with raw[:raw.rfind(b'\n')] (the +1 is gone). With no newline in the file rfind is -1, so the slice is raw[:-1], which still ends in a cut character: the inner decode fails and _read_lines raises StoreError instead of treating the lone first record as a write in progress. A reader landing while the first record of a thread or task log is being written with a non-ASCII character in it therefore fails (read_log, transcript, journal). With an earlier newline the slice only loses that newline and the result is the same, so every multi-line case still passes
ground_truth.location: jarvis/v2/stores.py _read_lines (text = raw[:raw.rfind(b'\n')].decode('utf-8') in the except UnicodeError branch)
ground_truth.evidence: probe (HOME=$(mktemp -d) PYTHONPATH=<tree> python probe.py): write a one-record log whose last byte is missing ('{"t": 1.5, "role": "you", "text": "caf\u00e9 \u2713' encoded as UTF-8, minus its final byte, so it is cut inside the check mark, no newline) to log.jsonl and call jarvis.v2.stores._read_lines.
